verdict.rationale: The only relevant evidence is that Kling publishes two regional API endpoints, a Global one in Singapore and a China one in Beijing. That gives API users a regional choice, but nothing says whether this controls where data is stored, so data residency is implied rather than documented. Missing for 10: explicit data-residency or storage-location documentation, region choice for web/app (non-API) users, guarantees that data stays in the chosen region, and independent corroboration.
